answer: Trust-flow gating: reward is nectar that can only drip inward along attestation edges rooted at a small set of established anchor identities. A new agent earns nothing until a non-kin anchor vouches for it, and that voucher is capped and decays over epochs. Sybils spawned off one host form an isolated juniper-thicket with no inbound edge from any real anchor, so the whole cluster settles to zero flow. To win, an attacker must first corrupt genuine anchors, and each capture costs real slashable standing, so forging N fakes costs N anchor-captures, not N cheap signups.
